title: 冬眠明けで山にいるばずのクマが市街地に出没、４月の目撃は昨年の４倍…専門家「鈴で存在アピールより建物避難を」
extracted_text:
冬眠明けでまだ山にいるはずのクマが、東北、北陸の市街地に出没している。宮城、秋田、福島の各県では、４月の目撃件数は前年の４倍前後。大型連休で人の行き来が増える中、識者は「人に慣れたクマが出ているとみられ、見かけたら建物内に避難して」と呼びかけている。
東北各県の４月のクマ目撃件数（速報値、集計中の岩手を除く）は、青森、秋田、宮城、福島の４県で前年より増加。青森が前年比２・３倍の１０５件、宮城が同４・５倍の１１６件、秋田が同４・６倍の３８９件、福島が同３・９倍の１１２件と、ハイペースで目撃情報が集まっている。
そのため、各県が住民への注意喚起で運用しているクマ出没警報・特別注意報は４月中に６県全てが発表。いずれも過去最速だった。
４月の出没で衝撃的だったのは、福島県郡山市と仙台市のケースだ。
郡山市で６～８日に現れたクマは、ＪＲ郡山駅から約３キロ西の住宅地の奥深くに侵入。市は花火や放水などで追い払いを試みた。最終的に高速道路のり面に逃げたところを緊急銃猟で駆除したが、対応した市農業生産流通課の結城弘勝課長（５４）は「こんな出没は初めて。追い払いで街中に向かわせる恐れもあり、リスク回避が難しかった」と振り返る。
１７～１９日に仙台市青葉区に現れたクマは、緊急銃猟が困難な市街地を徘徊。最後は宮城県庁から約８００メートル北西のマンション敷地の茂みに１０時間以上とどまり、麻酔銃で捕獲された。隣接する住宅の植木には爪痕も残され、住人女性（８６）は「こんな都会にクマが来るなんてびっくりだし、怖い」と声を震わせた。
異例の出没は東北以外にも広がり、富山市では４月２９日、犬の散歩中だった４０歳代女性がクマに襲われ、顔や首などを負傷。翌日駆除された。場所は神通川の河口に近い平野部の住宅街で、河川敷が侵入経路になった可能性があるという。
出没したのは３件とも雄の成獣（体長約１・５メートル）だった。クマの行動に詳しい東京農工大の小池伸介教授（生態学）は「昨秋、人里の良さを覚え、再び出てきている可能性がある。遭遇時はクマ鈴などで存在をアピールするより、車や建物に避難する方が安全だ」と話す。
外出時の準備については「現在の出没地域は、昨秋の出没地域と重なる部分がある。旅行先の昨秋の出没地域も確認した方がいい」とアドバイスする。
大型連休のさなか、民間事業者や自治体はクマへの警戒を強めている。
キャンプ場を備える岩手県釜石市の観光施設「根浜シーサイド」では、利用客にクマスプレーを無料で貸与。４月中旬からは「みちのく潮風トレイル」を歩くハイカーにも、大音量が鳴る「クマ除けホーン」とスプレーの貸与を始めた。観光シーズンに合わせた措置で、スタッフの佐藤奏子さん（４７）は「いざという時に身を守れるようにしてほしい」と訴える。
貸し切りバスなどを運行する仙南交通（仙台市）は、全車両にクマ対策スプレーを常備。連休中も乗客の乗降時は乗務員がスプレーを携行して警戒にあたる。
秋田県鹿角市は山菜採り中の人身被害をなくそうと、１日から６月末まで、過去に被害が多発している十和田高原地区を「入山禁止」に。バリケードを１１か所に設置した。
福島市は、クマの移動経路とみられる河川沿いにクマが嫌がる音を出す装置を昨年から設置。センサーがクマを感知すると音を出して追い返す。４月には８台を追加し、計１４台が稼働中だ。昨年は設置場所から下流域で目撃情報がなかったという。
（詳しくはこちら）
translated_text:
Bears that should still be in the mountains after waking from hibernation are appearing in urban areas in the Tohoku and Hokuriku regions. In Miyagi, Akita, and Fukushima prefectures, the number of bear sightings reported in April is roughly four times that of the previous year. With the consecutive public holidays driving increased movement of people, experts are urging the public to seek shelter inside buildings if they spot a bear.

The number of bear sightings reported in April across Tohoku prefectures (preliminary figures, excluding Iwate, which is still compiling data) increased compared with the previous year across all four prefectures: Aomori saw 105 sightings, 2.3 times the previous year; Miyagi had 116, a 4.5-fold increase; Akita recorded 389, a 4.6-fold jump; and Fukushima reported 112, nearly four times the prior year — with sightings pouring in at a rapid pace.

As a result, all six prefectures in the region issued bear-alert warnings for residents in April, the fastest timing on record for each.

Among April sightings, two cases in particular caused shockwaves.

A bear that appeared in Koriyama City from the 6th to the 8th ventured deep into a residential area roughly three kilometers west of JR Koriyama Station. The city attempted to drive it away using fireworks and water jets. The bear was ultimately eliminated by emergency firearms hunting after fleeing onto a highway embankment, but Yoeki Hiroshige, director of the city's Agricultural Production and Distribution Division (54), reflected: "This kind of sighting is a first for us. There was a risk that trying to drive it away could have sent it running into the town center, making risk avoidance difficult."

A bear that appeared in Aoba Ward, Sendai, from the 17th to the 19th roamed through a densely built-up area where emergency firearms hunting was impractical. It remained in the shrubs of a condominium complex roughly 800 meters northwest of the Miyagi Prefectural Government Office for more than ten hours before being captured with a tranquilizer dart. Claw marks were also left on the hedge of an adjacent house, and an 86-year-old female resident said, her voice trembling: "I can't believe a bear would come into the city like this. It's terrifying."

Unusual bear sightings have also spread beyond Tohoku. In Toyama City, a woman in her 40s out walking her dog was attacked by a bear on April 29, sustaining injuries to her face, neck, and other areas. The bear was eliminated the following day. The location was a residential neighborhood on flat land near the mouth of the Jinzu River, and the riverbank may have served as the bear's entry route.

All three confirmed bears were male adults, approximately 1.5 meters in body length. Professor Koike Shinsuke (ecology) of Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology, who studies bear behavior, said: "There is a possibility that last autumn they learned how good the human settlements were and have come back out. When encountering a bear, it is safer to seek shelter in a car or building than to try to announce your presence with a bear bell or other device."

On preparations when going out, he advised: "The current sightings overlap somewhat with areas where bears were active last autumn. It would be wise to check whether there were bear sightings in your travel destination last autumn."

In the midst of the consecutive holidays, private businesses and local governments are strengthening their vigilance against bears.

Nehama Seaside, a tourism facility in Kamaishi City, Iwate, which operates a campsite, is lending bear spray to visitors free of charge. From mid-April, the facility has also been providing hikers walking the Michinoku Shiokaze Trail with loud-sounding bear deterrent horns and spray. The measure is timed to the tourism season, and staff member Kaneko Saori (47) said: "We want people to be able to protect themselves when the moment comes."

Sennan Kotsu, a bus company in Sendai that operates chartered buses, has equipped all its vehicles with bear deterrent spray. During the holiday period, crew members carry the spray when passengers board and alight to maintain vigilance.

The city of Akita in the Towada region has designated the Towada Plateau area — where bear attacks have been frequent in the past — as off-limits to mountain vegetable gatherers from May 1 through the end of June. Concrete barriers have been erected at eleven locations.

Fukushima City has been installing devices that emit sounds bears dislike along riverbanks, which are believed to be bear travel routes, since last year. Sensors detect bears and sound to drive them away. In April, eight additional units were added, bringing the total to fourteen currently in operation. Last year, there were no bear sighting reports in areas downstream from the device locations.

title_en: Bears that should still be in mountains after hibernation are appearing in city areas; April sightings four times last year's rate... Expert: 'Seek shelter in buildings rather than use bells to announce presence'
